md_carderock.blurb: Carderock is a compact cliff-and-boulder area in Montgomery County, Maryland, on the strip between the Potomac River and the C&O Canal just outside Washington, DC. The cliffs are mica schist studded with quartz knobs, mostly around 35 feet tall and facing southwest. Top-roping is the main event: easy to moderate slabs and a few cracks, with trees above the cliff to rig from. Grades run from very easy up into the 5.12 range, with most of the climbing between 5.6 and 5.10. The boulders reward careful footwork on the quartz. Leading on gear is poorly regarded because the rock gives few good placements. Hades Heights and Jungle Cliffs hold most of the climbs, and Outlook Rocks leans toward bouldering. Spring and fall are kinder than the humid summer.

ma_gilbert_hills_state_park.blurb: Gilbert Hills State Park, also called F. Gilbert Hills State Forest, is a pine and oak woodland of roughly a thousand acres in Foxborough and Wrentham, Massachusetts, about three-quarters of the way along the road from Boston to Providence. The climbing is all bouldering: dozens of separate boulders and a few short cliffs spread through the trees, which makes it a place to wander between problems. Grades begin at V0 and stretch far up the scale, but the weight sits in the V1 to V6 range, so beginners and mid-level climbers have plenty to work on, with a small handful of very hard lines. The Trees and The Twins are the largest groupings, followed by Goat Rock and Phantom Tower.

nm_utopian_vistas.blurb: Utopian Vistas is a basalt cliff area in the Rio Grande Gorge, about 20 miles from Taos, New Mexico, sitting above the Rock Garden stretch of the river. The dark, pocketed volcanic rock gives vertical to overhanging lines, technical corners, roofs and thin cracks. Sport and trad routes are split almost evenly, and the grades cluster at 5.10 and 5.11, with a decent number of 5.9s and easier climbs and a handful at 5.12. The cliffs are organised into upper tiers, such as Utopian Vista Upper Tier and White Riot Wall Upper Tier, and a row of lower walls including John Nichol's Wall and Good Craic Wall. Freeze-thaw cycles are hard on the rock, so newer routes can shed holds and a helmet is wise.

tn_woodcock_cove.blurb: Woodcock Cove is a cliff near Dunlap in Sequatchie County, Tennessee, looking out over the Sequatchie Valley and roughly an hour from Chattanooga. The sandstone cliff line runs about a mile and includes big dihedral walls and a freestanding pillar, features that are unusual in the Southeast. Nearly everything is single pitch, and sport routes far outnumber trad. Grades run from the 5.6s up to 5.13, with the bulk between 5.10 and 5.12 and a useful block of moderates below that. The crag is divided into many short sections, among them The Distillery, The Red Baron Wall, The Dispensary and CBD Wall, so a day can be spent moving between several walls of similar character.

ab_crowsnest_pass.blurb: Crowsnest Pass sits in the southern Rockies of Alberta, reached through rolling foothills and ranch country. Two quite different styles share the valley. Frank Slide holds the most climbs, all bouldering, on sharp, clean limestone blocks left when the north face of Turtle Mountain collapsed in 1903; problems run from easy V0 up to a few very hard lines, with most between V0 and V3. Emerald Lake is a northeast-facing limestone cliff of mostly sport routes, single pitch and multipitch, with the better-known lines between 5.6 and 5.10a. Smaller spots such as Cleft Cave and Gargoyle add more sport climbing. Roped grades concentrate around 5.9 to 5.10, and trad is a small minority.

bc_aberdeen_columns.blurb: Aberdeen Columns is a crack-climbing crag in the Okanagan of interior British Columbia, near Vernon. The rock is polygonal basalt, in steep columns from about 12 to 25 metres tall, and it gives straight-in cracks from fingers to off-width on solid stone that takes cams and the odd nut. Nearly all of it is trad, with a few aid lines, and the grades run from easy up to the low 5.12s, with most routes at 5.9 and 5.10. The cliffs face west, so they stay shaded in the morning and take the sun until it sets. Aspen Pillars, Aberdeen Wall, Edwin Wall and Nicklen Wall hold most of the routes.
